newsitem.title: JAPAN: COFFEE - Japan traders calm over ACPC agreement.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE - Japan traders calm over ACPC agreement.

text.p: Japan's coffee traders reacted calmly on Thursday to a decision by bean producers to extend an agreement to limit their exports for one year, saying that the move had been widely expected.
"The ACPC's agreement was within our expectations, so we are not panicking," a coffee trader at a trade house said.

On Wednesday, world coffee markets surged amid news that the 14-nation Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) had reached an accord to limit export quotas at 52.75 million bags for one year starting July 1.
Earlier in the week, market talk that the ACPC might revise or scrap export quotas altogether had contributed to a bearish mood, traders said.

Japanese roasters are currently keeping a low profile in the physical coffee market, only buying nearby requirements in spot deals, expecting high global coffee prices to come down in the near future.
"Roasters are assuming the market will fall back at some stage as funds liquidate their long positions," a trader at another trade house said.
Traders also said they were doubtful whether Colombian exporters actually held as much as 500,000 60-kg bags of coffee.
Late Monday, Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation re-opened May/June coffee registrations for shipments of a maximum 500,000 60-kg bags by private exporters.
The federation said these consignments would be destined for Europe and Japan since export schedules to the United States had been fulfilled.
"Our first reaction (to the news) was to question whether they actually have 500,000 bags," the second trader said.
Some Japanese traders recently imported almost 150,000 bags of old crop Colombian coffee, in an attempt to secure prompt supplies but were not happy with the quality, industry officials said.

"Colombian (old crop) coffee's quality was worse than expectations. Local roasters are complaining," an official with a major roaster said. "So its doubtful how interested the Japanese will be in buying more Colombian beans," he said.
At the end of March, coffee stocks at Japanese warehouses totalled 67,030 tonnes, up by 26.7 percent from a year earlier, according to Agriculture Ministry data.
End-of-April coffee stock data will probably be available early next week, a ministry official said.
Japan's total green coffee imports in the first three months of this year totalled 85,784 tonnes, against 65,834 tonnes the previous year, according to the latest Finance Ministry data.
Japan is the world's third-largest coffee consumer after the United States and Germany.
